tagline: The app that puts the desktop on your screen
description:
**Xios** is the one app iOS sees. It appears on the Home Screen as **X11**, owns a Metal layer and the UIKit input surface, and renders nothing of its own: the compositor hands it an output IOSurface over a mach port, the app draws that as a Metal texture every frame, and your touches and keystrokes go back to the compositor. Nothing is streamed and nothing is copied.

The fullscreen flavors need it, so you normally do not install it directly: **xios-gnome**, **xios-kde**, and **xios-x11** pull it in through **xios-core**. The per-app **xios-native** flavor doesn't use it.

Open it and pick a desktop, or start one from the shell with `xios-session gnome` (or `kde`, `iosc`). Once a desktop is up:

- **three-finger tap** opens the Xios panel: desktop, screen size, apps, and other running displays under Advanced
- **two-finger tap** right-clicks
- **pinch** zooms to fit
- **swipe up from the lower edge** raises the iOS keyboard

The app is unsigned, so it needs **AppSync Unified** (from the https://cydia.akemi.ai/ repo) to launch. Rootless jailbreaks only (/var/jb), iOS/iPadOS 16 or newer, iPad.

changelog.notes: - Ships together with xios-launcher-tools 0.1.12: the picker and ioscd now agree on desktop-file ids
- Lets go of a display once its compositor is gone, so taps reach the desktop that is actually running instead of a stopped one

- Fixes a trackpad click that stayed held down, which made everything drag-select
- With a mouse or trackpad attached, the iPadOS pointer takes the desktop's cursor shape

- First packaged release: the display app now installs from the repo instead of being sideloaded
- Zero-copy IOSurface presentation through Metal, session and dimension picker, multi-display switching
- Touch, Pencil, hardware keyboard, and on-screen keyboard routed back to the display server
